title: Christmas Morning Corned Beef Hash
headnote: Corned beef hash has become the family’s post-present-opening tradition on Christmas morning — the hearty breakfast that comes after the gifts. “Can make w/o eggs ahead — reheat Xmas morning.” — Linda

quotes.text: Can make w/o eggs ahead — reheat Xmas morning.
quotes.span: “Can make w/o eggs ahead — reheat Xmas morning.” — Linda

items.raw: 1½ pounds Yukon Gold or russet potatoes (or 3 cups diced leftover boiled potatoes)
2 tablespoons neutral oil or bacon fat
2–2½ cups cooked corned beef, cut into ½-inch dice
2 sausage links, sliced — Linda often adds them; what kind?
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: If starting with raw potatoes, cut into ½-inch dice, cover with cold salted water, bring to a boil, and simmer 5 to 6 minutes, until just tender. Drain and spread out to steam dry. Leftover potatoes can go straight in.

steps.lead: Brown the sausage, then the onion.
steps.text: Heat the butter and oil in a large cast-iron or heavy nonstick skillet over medium heat. If using sausage, brown the slices first, 4 to 5 minutes, and lift them out. Cook the onion and pepper 5 to 7 minutes, until soft.

Add the potatoes and spread into an even layer. Press down with a spatula and leave them alone 5 to 6 minutes, until a deep brown crust forms on the bottom. Turn in sections and press again. Repeat once or twice.

Stir in the corned beef, the browned sausage, the garlic powder, and Worcestershire. Press flat again and cook without stirring 5 minutes more, until the beef crisps at the edges. Season with pepper; taste before adding salt, since corned beef is salty.

Make 6 wells in the hash with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Cover the pan and cook over medium-low 4 to 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still runny. Or fry or poach the eggs separately.
Scatter with parsley and bring the skillet to the table.

notes.label: Linda’s make-ahead
notes.text: make the hash without the eggs the day before. On Christmas morning, reheat it in the skillet, pressing it flat to re-crisp, then add the eggs.

notes.label: The crust is the point
notes.text: resist stirring. Every time you press and wait, you get more crisp brown bits.

notes.label: Canned corned beef
notes.text: break it into chunks and add it with the potatoes.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: ketchup, hot sauce, or a spoonful of hollandaise.

openQuestion: Linda’s notes suggest she makes the hash — is that right? And what kind of sausage goes in?
